question: Harold C Urey was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, in 1934:

options.text: for discovery in the chemistry of the transuranium elements
for the discovery of heavy hydrogen
for the discovery and development of conductive polymers
for the development of the density-functional theory

solution:
The correct answer is __**for the discovery of heavy hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harold C. Urey** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in **1934**.
 
• The award was given for his **discovery of heavy hydrogen**, also known as **deuterium**.
 
• Heavy hydrogen (**deuterium**) is an isotope of hydrogen with one neutron in addition to the single proton in the nucleus of the atom, making it heavier than regular hydrogen. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The discovery of deuterium was a breakthrough in the field of **isotopes**, contributing significantly to the understanding of atomic structures and nuclear chemistry.
 
• Urey’s discovery laid the foundation for advancements in **nuclear reactions** and studies of the behavior of isotopes in chemical processes. *Hence, the discovery is of paramount importance.*
 
• The discovery also had practical applications, such as in **nuclear power**, **thermonuclear reactions**, and as a tracer in **biological and chemical research.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Harold C. Urey:**

 
 
• **Harold Clayton Urey** (1893–1981) was an American physical chemist and a pioneer in the study of isotopes.
 
• He discovered **deuterium** in **1931** and subsequently received the **Nobel Prize** for this significant achievement.
 
• Urey’s work also contributed to the development of the **Manhattan Project**, which focused on nuclear weapon development during World War II.
 
 
 
• **About Heavy Hydrogen (Deuterium):**
 
 
• **Deuterium** is a naturally occurring isotope of hydrogen, with a nucleus composed of one proton and one neutron.
 
• It is found in small amounts in **water molecules**, which are referred to as **heavy water** when enriched with deuterium.
 
• **Applications:** Used in **nuclear reactors**, **biological research**, and **spectroscopic studies**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Nobel Prize in Chemistry:**
 
 
• The Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognizes **groundbreaking discoveries** that contribute to the advancement of science and practical applications globally.
 
• Urey’s recognition highlighted the importance of **isotope chemistry** in modern scientific progress.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Characteristics of Isotopes:**

 
 
• **Isotopes** are variants of elements with the same atomic number but different mass numbers due to the presence of varying numbers of neutrons.
 
• **Deuterium** is a stable isotope of hydrogen and does not undergo radioactive decay.
 
 
 
• **Heavy Water (D₂O):**
 
 
• Heavy water is water in which the hydrogen atoms have been replaced with **deuterium atoms**.
 
• **Uses:** Heavy water is a crucial moderator in **nuclear reactors** and is used in **neutron scattering experiments.**
